29 The diagram shows a stationary wave on a stretched spring at an instant in time.
P
Q
stretched
spring
Two particles on the spring, P and Q, are shown.
Which statement about the vibrations of P and Q is correct?
A
They have different frequencies.
B
They have the same amplitudes.
C
They have different periods.
D
They are always in phase.

hints: Look at where P and Q sit on the diagram: P is at the crest and Q is on the same upper loop above the dashed equilibrium line.
Recall that in a stationary wave the amplitude varies with distance from a node but the frequency and period are the same for all particles.
Recall that all particles between two adjacent nodes in a stationary wave move up and down together, reaching maximum displacement at the same instant.
walkthrough: Identify the pattern: the diagram shows one instant of a stationary wave with P at maximum displacement and Q on the same hump above the dashed equilibrium position.
State the stationary-wave rules: all particles except at nodes vibrate with the same frequency $f$ and period $T = 1/f$, but with amplitude that is maximum at an antinode and zero at a node.
Apply amplitude to P and Q: P is nearer the antinode than Q, so P vibrates with larger amplitude than Q.
Apply phase: particles in the same loop between adjacent nodes always move in the same direction at the same time and pass through equilibrium together, so their phase difference is $0$.
Therefore P and Q have the same frequency, same period, different amplitudes, and are always in phase. This is option D

A.explanation: In a stationary wave all vibrating particles complete oscillations in the same time, so P and Q have the same frequency $f$.

B.explanation: Amplitude in a stationary wave depends on position, and P at the crest has larger amplitude than Q further down the slope.

C.explanation: Period $T = 1/f$ is the same for all points in the stationary wave, so P and Q do not have different periods.

D.explanation: P and Q lie in the same loop between the same adjacent nodes, so they pass through equilibrium together and are in phase.
